key_insight: lPINN turns a PINN into a reduced-order model by pretraining nonlinear basis functions offline and solving each new PDE instance by optimizing only a final linear layer under physics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This can cut online inference cost by 10x to 1000x+ while improving accuracy for forward and inverse PDE problems, making physics-based ML more practical for fast simulation and parameter estimation.
method: Learn continuous neural basis functions from an ensemble of numerical solutions in an offline stage.
Pretrain basis functions using solution data plus derivative information or physics residuals.
Freeze the basis online and fit only the linear coefficients using governing-equation, boundary/initial, regularization, and observation terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors than vanilla PINNs and online speedups ranging from about one to more than three orders of magnitude, especially with limited data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the offline training ensemble, so the learned basis may generalize less well if new problems differ substantially from the pretrained solution family.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
